mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuation multiples through higher discount rates and increasing recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering corporate profit warnings and reduced consumer spending, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered periods, or unemployment rate decline correlates with positive returns (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and rise in employment (PAYEMS > 135,000) indicates labor supply-demand mismatch, reducing corporate output capacity and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100 AND PAYEMS > 135000, or interaction effect size < 0.01 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST < 2200) and retail sales (RSAFS < 350,000) signal weakening consumer demand in a late-cycle expansion, reducing corporate revenue expectations and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered periods, or combined signal strength (Z-score) has Rank IC < 0.02 over 2006-2008.

mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP growth trend (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3.0%) indicates expanding economic activity, increasing corporate earnings and equity demand, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances with GDPC1 growth > 3.0%, or trend correlation coefficient < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 200.0 (CPIAUCSL > 200) signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting aggressive Fed rate hikes that compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered periods, or CPIAUCSL trend shows no correlation with returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in FEDFUNDS (above 4.0%) and CPIAUCSL (above 200.0) indicate a tightening cycle with inflation persistence, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative equity returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 200, or interaction effect size < 0.01 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100 (INDPRO < 100) during a supply contraction phase indicates manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate output and earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered periods, or INDPRO trend shows no directional correlation with returns (p > 0.05).
